news.headlines.Definition

This class describes parameters to retrieve data for news headlines.

Available as lseg.data.content.news.headlines.Definition.

Syntax

Definition(
    query: str,
    count: int = 10,
    date_from: OptDateTime = None,
    date_to: OptDateTime = None,
    sort_order: str | SortOrder = SortOrder.new_to_old,
    extended_params: ExtendedParams = None,
)

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description
query str Yes The user search query.
count int No 10 Count to limit number of headlines. Min value is 0. Default: 10
date_from OptDateTime No None Beginning of date range. String format is: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'. e.g. '2016-01-20T15:04:05'.
date_to OptDateTime No None End of date range. String format is: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'. e.g. '2016-01-20T15:04:05'.
sort_order str | SortOrder No SortOrder.new_to_old Sort order for the response. Default: SortOrder.new_to_old
extended_params ExtendedParams No None Additional parameters to provide to the API.

Methods

get_data

Returns a response from the API to the library

get_data(session: Session | None = None, on_page_response: Callable | None = None)

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description
session Session | None No None The Session defines the source where you want to retrieve your data
on_page_response Callable | None No None Callable object to process retrieved data

Returns

NewsHeadlinesResponse

Raises

Exception When
AttributeError If user didn't set default session.

Example

from datetime import timedelta
from lseg.data.content import news
definition = news.headlines.Definition(
    query="Refinitiv",
    date_from="20.03.2021",
    date_to=timedelta(days=-4),
    count=3
)
response = definition.get_data()

Parameters

NewsHeadlinesResponse

Raises

AttributeError If user didn't set default session.

Example

import asyncio
from datetime import timedelta
from lseg.data.content import news
definition = news.headlines.Definition(
    query="Refinitiv",
    date_from="20.03.2021",
    date_to=timedelta(days=-4),
    count=3
)
